name: Fibrillary Astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Histological identification of fibrillary astrocytic cells with moderate cellularity and absence of necrosis or microvascular proliferation
MRI showing poorly defined, infiltrative, T2 hyperintense lesion without contrast enhancement
IDH1 or IDH2 mutation positivity supporting diagnosis of diffuse astrocytoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of fibrillary astrocytic morphology combined with characteristic MRI findings; molecular testing supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular markers such as IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion status assist in classification and prognosis.

searchTerms: gradual worsening of localized neurological problems
progressive weakness or numbness in one area

common.symptomName: Motor weakness localized to tumor site

occasional.symptomName: Nausea related to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea caused by high brain pressure
feeling sick due to intracranial pressure
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
imaging: MRI T2-weighted hyperintense, non-enhancing infiltrative lesion
Absence of necrosis or contrast enhancement on MRI
other: Histopathology showing fibrillary astrocytic cells with low mitotic activity
Lack of microvascular proliferation and necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Marked contrast enhancement with necrosis on MRI
Histopathology showing microvascular proliferation and necrosis

redFlags: New onset seizures in adult without prior history
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Ostrom QT et al. CBTRUS Statistical Report: Primary Brain and Other Central Nervous System Tumors Diagnosed in the United States, 2014-2018
Weller M et al. EANO guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of diffuse gliomas of adulthood. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2021
